claim: The ORd model was selected by a panel of experts as the model best suited for regulatory purposes.
source: Consequently, ORd was selected by a panel of experts as the model best suited for regulatory purposes (Dutta et al., 2017a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dutta et al., 2017a

claim: The plateau of the action potential is significantly higher in the ORd model than in experimental data used for ORd model construction.
source: Firstly, the plateau of the action potential (AP) is significantly higher in the ORd model than in experimental data used for ORd model construction (O'Hara et al., 2011; Britton et al., 2017) and in data from additional studies using human cardiomyocytes (Coppini et al., 2013; Jost et al., 2013).
evidence: Comparison with experimental data from multiple studies cited

claim: The dynamics of accommodation of the AP duration to heart rate acceleration show only limited agreement with a comparable experimental dataset in the ORd model.
source: Secondly, the dynamics of accommodation of the AP duration (APD) to heart rate acceleration, which are known to be modulated by sodium dynamics, show only limited agreement with a comparable experimental dataset (Franz et al., 1988; O'Hara et al., 2011).
evidence: Comparison with experimental data from Franz et al., 1988 and O'Hara et al., 2011

claim: Simulations of sodium current block have an inotropic effect in the ORd model, increasing the amplitude of the calcium transient.
source: Thirdly, we identify that simulations of the sodium current block has an inotropic effect in the ORd model, increasing the amplitude of the calcium transient, in disagreement with its established negatively inotropic effect in experimental/clinical data (encainide, flecainide, and TTX) (Gottlieb et al., 1990; Tucker et al., 1982; Legrand et al., 1983; Bhattacharyya and Vassalle, 1982).
evidence: Simulation results compared with experimental/clinical data from multiple cited studies

claim: Sodium current blockers have a negatively inotropic effect in experimental/clinical data.
source: Thirdly, we identify that simulations of the sodium current block has an inotropic effect in the ORd model, increasing the amplitude of the calcium transient, in disagreement with its established negatively inotropic effect in experimental/clinical data (encainide, flecainide, and TTX) (Gottlieb et al., 1990; Tucker et al., 1982; Legrand et al., 1983; Bhattacharyya and Vassalle, 1982).
evidence: Supported by multiple experimental/clinical studies cited

claim: AP plateau potential, APD adaptation and response to sodium current block have strong dependencies on sodium and calcium dynamics.
source: All those properties, namely AP plateau potential, APD adaptation and response to sodium current block, have strong dependencies on sodium and calcium dynamics.
evidence: Based on established understanding of cardiac electrophysiology

claim: The L-type calcium current formulation requires in-depth re-evaluation given its fundamental role in determining the AP, the calcium transient and sodium homeostasis through the Na/Ca exchanger.
source: We specifically focus on an in-depth re-evaluation of the L-type calcium current (ICaL) formulation, given its fundamental role in determining the AP, the calcium transient and sodium homeostasis through the Na/Ca exchanger.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of ICaL's role in cardiac electrophysiology

claim: The ToR-ORd model can reproduce all key depolarisation, repolarisation and calcium dynamics properties in healthy ventricular cardiomyocytes, under drug block, and in key diseased conditions.
source: Our aim for simulations using the ToR-ORd model is to be able to reproduce all key depolarisation, repolarisation and calcium dynamics properties in healthy ventricular cardiomyocytes, under drug block, and in key diseased conditions such as hyperkalemia (central to acute myocardial ischemia), and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence: Statement of research aim, validated through subsequent results

claim: The recordings used for calibration were obtained in human ventricular preparations primarily using measurements with microelectrode recordings, unipolar electrograms, and monophasic APs.
source: The recordings in were obtained in human ventricular preparations primarily using measurements with microelectrode recordings, unipolar electrograms, and monophasic APs, therefore avoiding photon scattering effects or potential dye artefacts present in optical mapping experiments.
evidence: Description of experimental methodology used in calibration data

claim: The ToR-ORd model was calibrated to manifest depolarisation of resting membrane potential in response to an IK1 block.
source: In addition, the ToR-ORd model was calibrated to manifest depolarisation of resting membrane potential in response to an IK1 block, based on evidence in a range of studies summarised in Dhamoon and Jalife (2005).
evidence: Calibration criterion based on evidence from cited study

claim: Simulations with the existing versions of the ORd model failed to fulfil key criteria such as AP morphology, calcium transient duration, several properties of the L-type calcium current, negative inotropic effect of sodium blockers, or the depolarising effect of IK1 block.
source: Simulations with the existing versions of the ORd model failed to fulfil key criteria such as AP morphology, calcium transient duration, several properties of the L-type calcium current, negative inotropic effect of sodium blockers, or the depolarising effect of IK1 block.
evidence: Results from simulations evaluating ORd model against calibration criteria

claim: Parameter optimisation using a multiobjective genetic algorithm was unable to fulfil key criteria such as AP and Ca morphology, and the effect of sodium and calcium block on calcium transient amplitude and APD with ORd-based models.
source: However, simulations with the ORd-based models were unable to fulfil key criteria such as AP and Ca morphology, and the effect of sodium and calcium block on calcium transient amplitude and APD, respectively.
evidence: Results from optimization attempts on ORd model

claim: The ToR-ORd model follows the general ORd structure.
source: The ToR-ORd model follows the general ORd structure (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1A

claim: The cardiomyocyte is subdivided into several compartments: main cytosolic space, junctional subspace, and the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
source: The cardiomyocyte is subdivided into several compartments: main cytosolic space, junctional subspace, and the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR, further subdivided into junctional and network SR).
evidence: Description of model structure

claim: Starting with the Luo-Rudy model of 1994, the driving force of ions via ICaL in cardiac models is modelled based on the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz flux equation.
source: However, starting with the Luo-Rudy model (LRd) of 1994 (Luo and Rudy, 1994), the driving force of ions via ICaL in cardiac models is modelled based on the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz (GHK) flux equation.
evidence: Historical statement about cardiac modeling practice, supported by citation

claim: The Luo-Rudy model uses γo = 0.341 for extracellular space and γi = 1 for the intracellular space.
source: The Luo-Rudy model and other Rudy-family models use γo = 0.341 for extracellular space and γi = 1 for the intracellular space.
evidence: Description of parameter values used in existing models

claim: Models based on the Shannon model use 0.341 for both intracellular and extracellular space.
source: Models based on the Shannon model (Shannon et al., 2004) use 0.341 for both intracellular and extracellular space, but we were unable to find the motivation for this change.
evidence: Description of parameter values in Shannon model with citation

claim: The Davies equation extends the basic Debye-Hückel equation to be accurate for ionic concentrations found in living cells.
source: We used the Davies equation, which extends the basic Debye-Hückel equation to be accurate for ionic concentrations found in living cells (Mortimer, 2008):
evidence: Statement about Davies equation properties, supported by citation

claim: The Davies equation was shown to be accurate for I up to 0.5, unlike the basic Debye-Hückel equation, which is accurate for I up to 0.01 only.
source: This warrants the use of Davies equation, which was shown to be accurate for I up to 0.5, unlike the basic Debye-Hückel equation, which is accurate for I up to 0.01 only (Mortimer, 2008).
evidence: Statement about accuracy ranges of equations, supported by citation

claim: Both intracellular and extracellular activity coefficients generally lie between 0.61 and 0.66 in ToR-ORd simulations.
source: Throughout our simulations, both intracellular and extracellular activity coefficients generally lie between 0.61 and 0.66.
evidence: Results from ToR-ORd simulations

claim: The intracellular and extracellular activity coefficients are relatively similar.
source: Importantly, this estimate shows that the intracellular and extracellular activity coefficients are relatively similar (corresponding to the broadly similar total concentration of charged molecules), in contrast with the original values.
evidence: Inference from simulation results and biophysical reasoning

claim: There is a theoretical inconsistency in previous cardiac models: the Nernstian driving force is used to derive the activation curve, but the GHK driving force is then used to calculate ICaL.
source: However, we identified a theoretical inconsistency in previous cardiac models across species (e.g. Luo and Rudy, 1994; Hund et al., 2008; O'Hara et al., 2011; Shannon et al., 2004; Grandi et al., 2010; Carro et al., 2011): whereas the Nernstian driving force of (V-ECa) is used to derive the activation curve, the GHK driving force is then used to calculate ICaL.
evidence: Theoretical analysis of existing models with citations

claim: Experimental studies reporting the activation curve of ICaL generally use the Nernstian driving force of (V-ECa) with ECa being the experimentally measured reversal potential of approximately 60 mV.
source: Indeed, experimental studies reporting the activation curve of ICaL generally use the Nernstian driving force of (V-ECa) with ECa being the experimentally measured reversal potential of approximately 60 mV.
evidence: Description of experimental methodology in literature

claim: 20% of ICaL was placed in the main cytosolic space in the ToR-ORd model, consistent with the literature.
source: 20% of ICaL was placed in the main cytosolic space, consistent with the literature (Scriven et al., 2010).
evidence: Model design choice supported by citation

claim: Placing 20% of ICaL in the main cytosolic space increases the plateau-supporting capability of ICaL.
source: This increases the plateau-supporting capability of ICaL, given that the myoplasmic ICaL is subject to a weaker calcium-dependent inactivation than ICaL in the junctional subspace.
evidence: Mechanistic explanation based on biophysical reasoning

claim: ICaL block is known to shorten APD experimentally.
source: ICaL block is known to shorten APD experimentally (O'Hara et al., 2011) but resulted in a major APD prolongation in simulations instead.
evidence: Experimental observation supported by citation

claim: The ORd IKr formulation lacks activation that is consistent with relevant experimental data.
source: A mechanistic analysis revealed that this follows from the lack of ORd IKr activation, which is however not consistent with relevant experimental data (Lu et al., 2001).
evidence: Analysis of ORd model compared with experimental data from Lu et al., 2001

claim: The Lu-Vandenberg IKr model is based on extensive experimental data allowing the dissection of activation and recovery from inactivation.
source: The Lu-Vandenberg IKr model is based on extensive experimental data allowing the dissection of activation and recovery from inactivation and provided the best agreement with experimental data, specifically when considering the AP plateau potentials reported experimentally.
evidence: Description of Lu-Vandenberg model properties

claim: Following the inclusion of the Lu-Vandenberg IKr formulation, all models generated during model calibration exhibited APD shortening in response to ICaL block.
source: Following the inclusion of the Lu-Vandenberg IKr formulation, all models generated during model calibration exhibited APD shortening in response to ICaL block.
evidence: Results from model calibration simulations

claim: The INa current formulation was replaced by an alternative human-based formulation from Grandi et al., 2010.
source: The INa current formulation was replaced by an alternative human-based formulation (Grandi et al., 2010), given established limitations of the original model with regards to conduction velocity and excitability (O'Hara et al., 2011), comment on article from 05 Oct 2012).
evidence: Model design choice with citations supporting the rationale

claim: The IK1 model was replaced with the human-based formulation by Carro et al., 2011, as it was shown to be key for simulations of hyperkalemic conditions.
source: The IK1 model was replaced with the human-based formulation by Carro et al. (2011), as it was shown to be key for simulations of hyperkalemic conditions.
evidence: Model design choice with citation and rationale

claim: A reduction in IK1 results in hyperpolarisation of the cell in the baseline ORd model.
source: When evaluating the baseline ORd model against the selected criteria, we observed that a reduction in IK1 results in hyperpolarisation of the cell (from −88 to −88.16 mV at 1 Hz pacing).
evidence: Simulation results from ORd model evaluation

claim: IK1 reduction depolarises cells experimentally.
source: However, it is established that IK1 reduction depolarises cells experimentally (Dhamoon and Jalife, 2005).
evidence: Experimental observation supported by citation

claim: ToR-ORd manifests depolarization in response to IK1 block, consistent with experimental data.
source: Changes made during ToR-ORd calibration (predominantly the altered balance of currents during diastole and the inclusion of background chloride current) result in ToR-ORd manifesting depolarization in response to IK1 block, consistent with experimental data.
evidence: Simulation results compared with experimental data

claim: The AP morphology of the ToR-ORd is within or at the border of the interquartile range of the Szeged-ORd experimental data.
source: The AP morphology of the ToR-ORd is within or at the border of the interquartile range of the Szeged-ORd experimental data (Figure 2A).
evidence: Comparison of simulation results with experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The original ORd morphology overestimates plateau potentials, particularly during early plateau.
source: This is a major improvement compared to the original ORd morphology, which overestimates plateau potentials, particularly during early plateau (Figure 2A).
evidence: Comparison shown in Figure 2A

claim: The early plateau potential is around 20–23 mV in experimental recordings.
source: The fact that the early plateau potential is around 20–23 mV is clearly apparent from experimental recordings and is further corroborated by additional studies in human tissue samples (Jost et al., 2013, Figure 6) and isolated human cardiomyocytes (Coppini et al., 2013).
evidence: Experimental data from multiple cited studies

claim: When coupled in a fibre, ToR-ORd manifests conduction velocity of 65 cm/s, which is consistent with clinical data.
source: When coupled in a fibre, ToR-ORd manifests conduction velocity of 65 cm/s, which is consistent with clinical data (Taggart et al., 2000).
evidence: Simulation result compared with clinical data from citation

claim: Both time to peak calcium and duration of calcium transient at 90% recovery obtained with the ToR-ORd model are within the standard deviation of experimental data in isolated human myocytes.
source: Both time to peak calcium and duration of calcium transient at 90% recovery obtained with the ToR-ORd model are within the standard deviation of experimental data in isolated human myocytes (Coppini et al., 2013), whereas ORd slightly overestimated the calcium transient duration (Figure 2B).
evidence: Comparison of simulation results with experimental data shown in Figure 2B

claim: In cases of elevated ICaL, ORd reverses current direction towards positive values.
source: We observed that in cases of elevated ICaL (e.g. in midmyocardial cells), ORd reverses current direction towards positive values, which is an unexpected behaviour given its reversal potential of 60 mV.
evidence: Observation from simulations

claim: The ToR-ORd model yields negative ICaL values in conditions of elevated ICaL, consistent with it being an inward current.
source: Conversely, the ToR-ORd model yields negative ICaL values in such conditions, consistent with it being an inward current (Figure 2F).
evidence: Simulation results shown in Figure 2F

claim: The ToR-ORd model manifests a small reduction in calcium transient amplitude in response to combined partial INa and INaL block.
source: The ToR-ORd model manifests a small reduction in calcium transient amplitude (Figure 3C), unlike ORd, which gives a sizeable increase (Figure 3D); ToR-ORd is thus consistent with the observed negative inotropy of sodium blockers (Gottlieb et al., 1990; Tucker et al., 1982; Legrand et al., 1983; Bhattacharyya and Vassalle, 1982).
evidence: Simulation results shown in Figure 3C compared with experimental data from citations

claim: The ToR-ORd model shows negative inotropy for almost all combinations of INa and INaL blocks.
source: The ToR-ORd model shows negative inotropy for almost all combinations of blocks.
evidence: Results from systematic simulation of different block combinations

claim: ORd shows a general tendency for increased calcium transient amplitude in response to sodium current block.
source: Conversely, ORd shows a general tendency for increased calcium transient amplitude; a reduction occurs only when the sodium current block targets near-exclusively INaL.
evidence: Results from systematic simulation of different block combinations

claim: The ToR-ORd model manifests EADs at conditions used experimentally in nondiseased human endocardium.
source: The ToR-ORd model manifests EADs at conditions used experimentally in nondiseased human endocardium (Guo et al., 2011; Figure 4A).
evidence: Simulation results compared with experimental conditions from citation, shown in Figure 4A

claim: The amplitude of simulated EADs is 14 mV, which matches the maximum EAD amplitude shown by Guo et al. (2011).
source: The amplitude of simulated EADs is 14 mV (Figure 4B), which matches the maximum EAD amplitude shown by Guo et al. (2011).
evidence: Simulation result shown in Figure 4B compared with experimental data from citation

claim: Alternans in the ToR-ORd model is calcium-driven and appears via the same mechanism as in the ORd: sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium cycling refractoriness.
source: Alternans in the ToR-ORd model is calcium-driven and appears via the same mechanism as in the ORd: sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium cycling refractoriness (Tomek et al., 2018).
evidence: Mechanistic analysis with citation

claim: The peak APD alternans amplitude in ToR-ORd is 12 ms, which matches the value 11 ± 2 ms reported in human hearts without a structural disease.
source: The peak APD alternans amplitude (difference in APD between consecutive beats) is 12 ms, which is matches the value 11 ± 2 ms reported in human hearts without a structural disease (Koller et al., 2005).
evidence: Simulation result compared with experimental data from citation

claim: The predictions produced by the ToR-ORd model for drug action are in good agreement with experimental data.
source: The predictions produced by the ToR-ORd model are in good agreement with experimental data, particularly given the lack of optimisation towards this result.
evidence: Comparison of simulation results with experimental data

claim: Models in both ToR-ORd populations are stable under significant perturbation of ionic conductances.
source: Models in both populations are stable under significant perturbation of ionic conductances, which supports the robustness of the model (Figure 7A).
evidence: Results from population of models simulations shown in Figure 7A

claim: Prediction of the risk of drug-induced Torsades de Pointes using ToR-ORd population yielded 87% accuracy (54 out of 62 compounds correct).
source: Prediction of the risk of drug-induced Torsades de Pointes based on simulated drug-induced repolarisation abnormalities using ToR-ORd population yielded similar results to the original study, with predicted risk being correct for 54 out of 62 compounds (87% accuracy).
evidence: Results from drug safety prediction simulations

claim: High-dose Mexiletine led to formation of many EADs in ORd, but not in ToR-ORd.
source: High-dose Mexiletine led to formation of many EADs in ORd, but not in ToR-ORd (Figure 7B), highlighting the importance of the advances on sodium blockers presented in this work.
evidence: Comparison of simulation results shown in Figure 7B

claim: The elevation of extracellular potassium level led to an increase of the resting membrane potential and the decrease of AP upstroke amplitude in ToR-ORd simulations.
source: As shown in Figure 8A, the elevation of extracellular potassium level led to an increase of the resting membrane potential (RMP) and the decrease of AP upstroke amplitude.
evidence: Simulation results shown in Figure 8A

claim: The APD shortened under hyperkalemia in ToR-ORd simulations.
source: As a result of weaker upstroke and more depolarised RMP, the APD shortened under hyperkalemia; however, the ERPs were prolonged due to the stronger sodium channel inactivation caused by the elevation of RMP (Figure 8B).
evidence: Simulation results shown in Figure 8B

claim: The ERPs were prolonged under hyperkalemia due to the stronger sodium channel inactivation caused by the elevation of RMP in ToR-ORd simulations.
source: As a result of weaker upstroke and more depolarised RMP, the APD shortened under hyperkalemia; however, the ERPs were prolonged due to the stronger sodium channel inactivation caused by the elevation of RMP (Figure 8B).
evidence: Simulation results with mechanistic explanation shown in Figure 8B

claim: The ToR-ORd model successfully reproduced the longer post-repolarization refractoriness under hyperkalemia observed in experiments.
source: Therefore, this new model successfully reproduced the longer post-repolarization refractoriness under hyperkalemia observed in experiments, and it can be used in the simulations of re-entrant arrhythmia under acute ischemia.
evidence: Comparison of simulation results with experimental observations

claim: The original ORd model did not manifest postrepolarisation refractoriness without further modifications.
source: In this regard, it presents an improvement over the original ORd model, which did not manifest postrepolarisation refractoriness without further modifications (Dutta et al., 2017b).
evidence: Comparison with ORd model behavior, supported by citation

claim: The HCM variant of the ToR-ORd model corresponds to experimental data in the AP morphology, manifesting a significantly higher plateau potential and an overall APD prolongation.
source: The HCM variant of the computer model corresponds to experimental data in the AP morphology, manifesting a significantly higher plateau potential and an overall APD prolongation (Figure 8C).
evidence: Simulation results compared with experimental data shown in Figure 8C

claim: The calcium transient amplitude of the HCM model is slightly reduced, has longer time to peak, and a noticeably longer duration at 90% recovery.
source: The calcium transient amplitude of the HCM model is slightly reduced, has longer time to peak, and a noticeably longer duration at 90% recovery (Figure 8D), also consistent with the data by Coppini et al. (2013).
evidence: Simulation results compared with experimental data shown in Figure 8D

claim: The HCM variant of ToR-ORd model is more prone to the formation of EADs.
source: Ultimately, the HCM variant of our model is more prone to the formation of EADs (Figure 8E), as was shown experimentally (Coppini et al., 2013).
evidence: Simulation results compared with experimental data shown in Figure 8E

claim: The ECG from ToR-ORd simulations manifests a QRS duration of 80 ms (normal range 78 ± 8 ms), and a QT interval of 350 ms (healthy:<430 ms).
source: The ECG manifests a QRS duration of 80 ms (normal range 78 ± 8 ms), and a QT interval of 350 ms (healthy:<430 ms); all of these quantitative measurements are in the range of ECGs of healthy persons (Engblom et al., 2005; van Oosterom et al., 2000).
evidence: Simulation results compared with normal ranges from cited studies

claim: ECG morphology from ToR-ORd simulations showed normal features, such as R wave progression in the precordial leads from V1 to V6, isoelectric ST segment, and upright T waves in leads V2 to V6, with inverted T wave in aVR.
source: ECG morphology also showed normal features, such as R wave progression in the precordial leads from V1 to V6, isoelectric ST segment, and upright T waves in leads V2 to V6, with inverted T wave in aVR.
evidence: Description of simulation results showing normal ECG features

claim: The activation sequence in ToR-ORd whole-heart simulations is in agreement with Durrer et al. (1970).
source: Figure 9C shows the activation sequence is in agreement with Durrer et al. (1970).
evidence: Simulation results shown in Figure 9C compared with experimental data from citation

claim: The APD map from ToR-ORd simulations shows longer APD in the endocardium and the base, and shorter APDs in the epicardium and the apex.
source: The APD map shows longer APD in the endocardium and the base, and shorter APDs in the epicardium and the apex, respectively (Figure 9D).
evidence: Simulation results shown in Figure 9D

claim: The ToR-ORd model was developed using a defined set of calibration criteria and subsequently validated on features not considered during calibration.
source: The ToR-ORd model was developed using a defined set of calibration criteria and subsequently validated on features not considered during calibration to demonstrate its predictive power.
evidence: Description of model development methodology

claim: The reformulation of the L-type calcium current is broadly relevant and generally applicable to human and other species.
source: This article also unravels several important theoretical findings with implications for computational electrophysiology reaching beyond the ToR-ORd model and cardiac electrophysiology: firstly, the reformulation of the L-type calcium current, which is broadly relevant and generally applicable to human and other species, and secondly, the mechanistically guided replacement of IKr.
evidence: Statement about the generalizability of the theoretical findings

claim: The good response of the ToR-ORd model to sodium blockade is particularly noteworthy among the improved behaviours compared to the ORd model.
source: Among the improved behaviours compared to the state-of-the-art ORd model (O'Hara et al., 2011), the good response of the ToR-ORd model to sodium blockade is particularly noteworthy.
evidence: Evaluation of model improvements

claim: ToR-ORd predicts the negative inotropic effect of sodium blockade, consistent with data, unlike ORd, which suggests a strong pro-inotropic effect.
source: ToR-ORd predicts the negative inotropic effect of sodium blockade, consistent with data (Gottlieb et al., 1990; Tucker et al., 1982; Legrand et al., 1983; Bhattacharyya and Vassalle, 1982), unlike ORd, which suggests a strong pro-inotropic effect.
evidence: Comparison of simulation results with experimental data from citations

claim: The improvement in ToR-ORd follows from the relatively complex interplay of the theoretically driven reformulation of the L-type calcium current and data-driven changes to the AP morphology.
source: The improvement in ToR-ORd follows from the relatively complex interplay of the theoretically driven reformulation of the L-type calcium current and data-driven changes to the AP morphology.
evidence: Explanation of the mechanistic basis for model improvements

claim: Validation of a model using data not employed in model calibration is a central aspect of model credibility.
source: An important feature of a model is its predictive power, and validation of a model using data not employed in model calibration is a central aspect of model credibility (Pathmanathan and Gray, 2018; Carusi et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement about model validation methodology, supported by citations

claim: The fact that ToR-ORd manifests a wide range of behaviours consistent with experimental studies, even though it was not optimised for these purposes, suggests its generality and a large degree of credibility.
source: The fact that ToR-ORd manifests a wide range of behaviours consistent with experimental studies, even though it was not optimised for these purposes, suggests its generality and a large degree of credibility.
evidence: Inference from validation results

claim: Activation curve of the current in previous cardiac models was based on the use of Nernst driving force in experimental studies, but the models then used Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz driving force to compute the current.
source: Activation curve of the current in previous cardiac models was based on the use of Nernst driving force in experimental studies, but the models then used Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz driving force to compute the current.
evidence: Analysis of existing modeling approaches

claim: This theoretical inconsistency is present in existing influential models of guinea pig, rabbit, dog, or human.
source: This yields a theoretical inconsistency present in existing influential models of guinea pig, rabbit, dog, or human, for example (Luo and Rudy, 1994; Hund et al., 2008; O'Hara et al., 2011; Shannon et al., 2004; Grandi et al., 2010; Carro et al., 2011).
evidence: Analysis of existing models with citations

claim: Updated ionic activity coefficients and activation of the L-type calcium current improve key features of the current observed in the study underlying the ORd L-type calcium current model.
source: Updated ionic activity coefficients and activation of the L-type calcium current improve key features of the current observed in the study underlying the ORd L-type calcium current model (Magyar et al., 2000), and strongly contribute to the improved reaction of the model to sodium blockade.
evidence: Comparison of model behavior with experimental data from citation

claim: Limitations of the ORd IKr model may be a result of the single-pulse voltage clamp protocol to characterise the current behaviour.
source: We noticed limitations of the ORd IKr model, which may be a result of the single-pulse voltage clamp protocol to characterise the current behaviour.
evidence: Speculation about the source of model limitations

claim: Approaches enabling the dissection of activation and recovery from inactivation based on more comprehensive experimental data may yield a more general and plausible model.
source: Approaches enabling the dissection of activation and recovery from inactivation based on more comprehensive experimental data, such as Lu et al. (2001) used in our work, may yield a more general and plausible model.
evidence: Reasoning about modeling approaches with citation

claim: The main future development of the ToR-ORd model will focus on the ryanodine receptor and the respective release from sarcoplasmic reticulum.
source: We anticipate that the main future development of the presented model will focus on the ryanodine receptor and the respective release from sarcoplasmic reticulum.
evidence: Statement about anticipated future work

claim: In most existing cardiac models, the equations governing the release depend directly on the L-type calcium current, rather than on the calcium concentration adjacent to the ryanodine receptors.
source: Similarly to most existing cardiac models, the equations governing the release depend directly on the L-type calcium current, rather than on the calcium concentration adjacent to the ryanodine receptors, which is the case in cardiomyocytes.
evidence: Description of current modeling approach compared with biological reality

claim: Future development of the ryanodine receptor model and calcium handling will extend the applicability of the model to other calcium-driven modes of arrhythmogenesis, such as delayed afterdepolarisations.
source: Future development of the ryanodine receptor model and calcium handling will extend the applicability of the model to other calcium-driven modes of arrhythmogenesis, such as delayed afterdepolarisations.
evidence: Statement about anticipated future improvements
